description: Variable initialisation, assignment as an expression, overwritable constants, and the finite clamp at the statement boundary.

cases.name: an uninitialized variable reads as 0
cases.note: Reading an unknown name is legal and yields 0. It is never an error, which is why a misspelled builtin fails silently.

cases.name: assignment is an expression returning the assigned value
pi and e read as the mathematical constants by default
pi and e are ORDINARY variables, so assignments to them stick
cases.note: ns-eel registers pi/e as plain prepopulated variables. Around 74 presets in the bundled corpus overwrite one of them, so treating them as read-only constants breaks real content.

cases.name: a non-finite value is clamped to 0 when stored
cases.note: Here 1/0 is already 0 by the division guard, so x is 5. The clamp exists because expression state persists across frames: one unclamped Infinity poisons a variable for the preset's lifetime.

cases.name: variable names are case-insensitive
cases.note: ns-eel is case-insensitive: `contVol` and `contvol` are one variable, and `Zoom = 1.02` sets the `zoom` state field. Identifier reads normalise to lowercase, so a store that keeps the writer's casing silently disagrees with every read. Eight presets in the bundled corpus depend on this (six spell `contVol`/`contvol` inconsistently, two do the same with X1/Y1).
